scope.primary_question: Can the prior P5 G7 failure be repaired with two independent timing sources, including a primary or official product-linked 2028-2035 trigger, without substituting generic host-system growth for the product job?

binding_interpretation.g7: A source dated in the 2028-2035 interval is necessary but not sufficient. The record must also support a named 2030-2034 product-category demand, procurement, regulation, capacity, roadmap, or customer-investment trigger; a generic host buildout or an R&D possibility is not a trigger.
binding_interpretation.g1: Two independent demand sources are sufficient when one is a primary buyer, procurement, filing, or direct-customer record; an order for the proposed startup itself is not required.
binding_interpretation.source_independence: A company press release and SEC filing about the same purchase are one underlying demand event even when they are separate canonical works.
binding_interpretation.truthfulness_rule: A failed repair remains failed even if passing it would help portfolio quotas.

proposed_selection_effect.P3R2-E-04: HOLD after gate repair; still architecture-sensitive and only 51.0/100 proposed.
proposed_selection_effect.P3R2-D-19: KILL for final-gate purposes; preserve as a strong-demand near miss.
proposed_selection_effect.P3R2-A-02: KILL; no named post-launch MVDC-breaker socket.
proposed_selection_effect.P3R2-A-22: KILL; G7 and the existing G2 defect both remain fatal.
proposed_selection_effect.P3R2-A-21: KILL; the port records buy lower-power distributed charging, not the preserved 1.5-6 MW MCS product.

records.concept_short: Distributed composite-flywheel kinetic buffers for off-grid AI power plants

timing_source_assessment.window_date: deliveries, testing, and takeover from H2 2027 through 2028
timing_source_assessment.product_job_linkage: The SEC filing proves $505M of generation equipment for data-center and distributed-power projects but does not name SHIELDX or flywheel buffering.
timing_source_assessment.reason: The 2028 date is in range, but the filing alone is host-equipment procurement and ends before the 2030 launch.

timing_source_assessment.window_date: deliveries commence H2 2027; installed architecture has a 20+ year operating lifecycle
timing_source_assessment.product_job_linkage: Exact: the Liberty release says Piller SHIELDX flywheel architecture absorbs sub-second AI load steps up to 30 percent.
timing_source_assessment.reason: It supplies exact product linkage and a 2028 delivery when read with the filing, but it is the same transaction and does not name a new 2030-2034 purchase.

timing_source_assessment.product_job_linkage: NERC records a 50 MW block within a 200 MW AI training center changing at 1.9 per-unit per second for about 250 ms, directly validating the transient job.
timing_source_assessment.reason: It proves present pain but provides no dated post-launch flywheel requirement.

records.g7_rationale: Two exact named buyers have now bought Piller-linked flywheel stabilization, but both equipment waves deliver by 2028. The 20+ year lifecycle preserves installed demand while also entrenching Piller. No independent named 2030-2034 customer procurement, regulation, or capacity event creates a startup entry socket at launch.
records.window_risk: The category is being vertically bundled now by Bergen, Piller, and Liberty's Forte/Tempo platform; rack-level supercapacitors, batteries, and software smoothing may remove the residual niche before 2030.

G1.rationale: Existing E-Finity/Piller procurement plus the independent Liberty purchase are two exact named-buyer demand events.

G4.rationale: Piller/Active Power, Stornetic, Liberty Tempo, BESS, and supercapacitors are named. A DC-native composite rotor optimized for residual microcycles is non-cosmetic, but it is unproved and the incumbent is already bundled.

G6.rationale: US civilian industrial base case; rotating-machinery containment, UL/IEEE interconnection, and facility safety need qualification, with no prohibited cross-border route required.

records.market_route: Only credible route is paid measurement followed by an OEM/EPC co-development or white-label agreement with an off-grid power-plant integrator; direct displacement of the incumbent is not a base case.

decisive_experiment.title: Measured residual AI-power spectrum and substitution economics
decisive_experiment.dependency: Signed synchronized access to an AI rack or power shelf and its generator or islanded test bus.
decisive_experiment.pass_bar: At least 1,000 representative transitions; rack controls leave a residual spectrum; modeled lifetime cost at least 30 percent below Piller or BESS-supercap; at least 100 modules per year addressable.
decisive_experiment.kill_bar: Shelf controls erase the niche, cost advantage is below 30 percent, or no site grants access.

proposed_score_change.reason: The new exact order strengthens confidence in already-high demonstrated demand but does not repair launch timing or whitespace.

records.concept_short: High-density cryogenic interconnect loader with co-packaged 4 K readout front-end

timing_source_assessment.independent_event: DOE National QIS Research Centers second phase
timing_source_assessment.window_date: November 2025 award selection for up to five years, extending through approximately 2030
timing_source_assessment.product_job_linkage: DOE assigns SQMS to new refrigeration methods and technologies for connecting many quantum processors, explicitly to lay groundwork for quantum data centers.
timing_source_assessment.reason: Named official program, exact cryogenic/interconnect work, and an award period reaching 2030; outyear funding remains contingent on appropriations and negotiations.

timing_source_assessment.product_job_linkage: IBM explicitly states Blue Jay requires new control-electronics and cryogenics infrastructure, the same hard systems boundary addressed by the loader.
timing_source_assessment.reason: Primary customer roadmap with exact 2029 and 2033 milestones and explicit control/cryogenic infrastructure demand.

records.g7_rationale: DOE's renewed SQMS mission reaches about 2030 and explicitly funds refrigeration and processor connection, while IBM's primary roadmap makes client systems available in 2029 and says its 2033+ system requires new control electronics and cryogenics. These are independent, product-linked triggers. Marginality remains because IBM's modular architecture could reduce external channels and both roadmaps are contingent.
records.repaired_launch_thesis: Use 2026-2028 to validate a modular 4 K interconnect/control segment and obtain a refrigerator-OEM interface; use 2029 DOE/IBM-class integration evidence to launch in 2030 into funded national-lab systems and post-Starling builders. Preserve a loader product only if customer roadmaps retain at least a 1,000-channel external socket; otherwise pivot the same cold-electronics package to modular quantum-compute interconnects or kill.
records.window_risk: On-chip multiplexing, optical cryo-links, SFQ control, or IBM-style modular links may internalize the I/O problem before 2030; export licensing constrains Taiwan/Korea work.

G1.rationale: DOE's named five-center $625M renewal is a primary official instrument with exact cryogenic/interconnect work; Fermilab-Qblox QICK and IBM's roadmap are independent category evidence. No loader order is claimed.

G4.rationale: Delft Circuits, Bluefors, SEEQC, IBM in-house architectures, and room-temperature control vendors are named. Co-qualified harness, mux, and LNA performance per refrigerator heat budget is non-cosmetic but architecturally vulnerable.

G6.rationale: The US-first base case is viable. BIS quantum/cryo controls and deemed-export screening must be completed before Taiwan/Korea transfers; those routes cannot be assumed.

exact_competitors: IBM and other in-house modular-link or cold-control architectures
Keysight and Quantum Machines room-temperature control stacks
records.market_route: US-first paid co-development with SQMS or another DOE QIS center plus a refrigerator OEM; TW/KR manufacturing or test work is optional and license-gated, not the base case.

decisive_experiment.title: Post-2029 external-I/O architecture socket test
decisive_experiment.dependency: No assumed partner access; confidential roadmap disclosure and paid co-development are required outcomes.
decisive_experiment.pass_bar: One written post-2029 external loader socket of at least 1,000 channels, one buyer funds at least 20 percent of the later demo, and a refrigerator OEM accepts the interface.
decisive_experiment.kill_bar: All roadmaps internalize I/O into cold electronics or modular links, no buyer funding, or no refrigerator interface.

proposed_score_change.reason: The two new primary timing records repair the timing-source defect but do not restore demand, competition, budget, elegance, or 10x deductions.

records.concept_short: Modular 1-35 kV hybrid solid-state circuit breaker for MVDC campuses and microgrids

timing_source_assessment.window_date: December 2025 report labels MVDC distribution Future greater than 5 years, implying after 2030
timing_source_assessment.product_job_linkage: Exact: PNNL says the future MVDC design requires cables, busbars, switchgear, and circuit breakers.
timing_source_assessment.reason: This is an unnamed research architecture and maturity warning, not a customer roadmap, project, purchase, or deployment commitment.

timing_source_assessment.product_job_linkage: EPRI projects data centers at 9-17 percent of US electricity by 2030 but does not specify MVDC distribution or standalone breakers.
timing_source_assessment.reason: Generic host-system growth cannot repair a product-specific protection gate.

records.g7_rationale: PNNL newly provides excellent product linkage and places MVDC data centers after 2030, but explicitly as a distant architecture with no named buyer or field deployment. EPRI's 2030 data-center buildout is generic. No named 2030-2034 standalone-breaker design-in survives.
records.window_risk: Point-to-point LVDC or MV solid-state-transformer architectures may defer or remove a standalone MVDC breaker; Hitachi, Eaton, Siemens, GE, DG Matrix, and Atom Power can bundle protection before the architecture becomes commercial.

G1.rationale: ARPA-E BREAKERS/DC work and PNNL's exact architecture establish category need, but no named hyperscaler has committed to buying a standalone 1-35 kV breaker.

G4.rationale: Hitachi Energy, Eaton, Siemens, GE, DG Matrix, and Atom Power are named; modular hybrid interruption is non-cosmetic, but protection may be bundled inside converters.

G6.rationale: No export prohibition is apparent. The unresolved US certification, arc/energy containment, selective coordination, and system-acceptance regime is a material route risk.

exact_competitors: Siemens and GE project-integrated DC protection
DG Matrix and Atom Power solid-state power platforms
records.market_route: A DC-GRIDS performer or hyperscaler owner's engineer must first specify a standalone breaker and sponsor high-energy testing; otherwise there is no merchant product route.

decisive_experiment.title: MVDC architecture and sponsored-breaker-socket gate
decisive_experiment.dependency: None assumed; the sponsor and design-in socket must emerge from the study.
decisive_experiment.pass_bar: Two system architects document a standalone breaker; one covers at least 80 percent of the 10 kV test; one breaker-specific 2030-2033 pilot requirement exists.
decisive_experiment.kill_bar: Architects select converter blocking or point-to-point topology, no standalone socket, or no sponsor funds testing.

proposed_score_change.reason: The official report improves problem definition but confirms maturity and customer-commitment gaps.

records.concept_short: Modular plasma destruction units for concentrated PFAS waste streams

timing_source_assessment.independent_event: EPA 2026 PFAS destruction and disposal guidance
timing_source_assessment.window_date: annual update cadence can reach 2028 and later
timing_source_assessment.product_job_linkage: The guidance covers AFFF and treatment wastes but recognizes only thermal destruction, landfill, and underground injection as large-scale capacity options.
timing_source_assessment.reason: An annual review cadence is not plasma approval or procurement; it is adverse regulatory-maturity evidence.

timing_source_assessment.product_job_linkage: Exact plasma-vortex validation on undiluted AFFF, with greater than 99.99 percent destruction/mineralization, closed-loop, polishing, cost, and transition-to-DoD objectives.
timing_source_assessment.reason: The exact project completes before the window and promises only transition work if successful, not a post-2030 procurement.

records.g7_rationale: A new exact DoD field project validates the technical category, but it ends in 2027. EPA's recurring guidance does not recognize plasma as a large-scale option. The 2031 drinking-water deadline creates residuals but does not order plasma systems, so no product-specific 2030-2034 trigger exists.
records.window_risk: Onvector already holds the exact plasma-vortex program; EPA may continue preferring thermal destruction, landfill, underground injection, or competing SCWO/electrochemical routes.

G1.rationale: Paid DoD plasma work, the USAF/Onvector pilot, and ER24-8956 are direct exact-category demand events.

G2.rationale: The current packet still lacks sufficient eligible peer-reviewed support for load-bearing plasma energy, byproduct, and complete fluorine-mass-balance claims; the official project page is not peer review.

G4.rationale: Onvector, PyroGenesis, 374Water, Aquagga, and electrochemical routes are named. Modular verified treatment is non-cosmetic, but Onvector is already the closest exact incumbent.

G6.rationale: EPA's 2026 guidance does not recognize plasma among three large-scale options, so destruction verification, emissions/byproducts, fluoride capture, waste handling, and regulator acceptance remain unresolved.

exact_competitors: permitted thermal destruction and disposal routes
records.market_route: Only through a DoD remediation prime or SERDP/ESTCP transition program with regulator-accepted mass balance; municipal utilities are not a base case until the method is recognized.

decisive_experiment.title: Minimum honest real-feed plasma campaign
decisive_experiment.dependency: Existing plasma laboratory, DoD or prime observer, and accredited analytical subcontractor.
decisive_experiment.pass_bar: Greater than 99.99 percent destruction, at least 95 percent fluorine closure, below 50 kWh per kg-PFAS, five consecutive eight-hour runs, and a follow-on buyer letter.
decisive_experiment.kill_bar: Mass-balance gap over 5 percent, persistent byproducts, energy above threshold, material failure, or no buyer observer.

proposed_score_change.reason: New exact technical-program evidence does not cure G2, G7, regulatory acceptance, or incumbent capture.

records.concept_short: Ruggedized 1.5-6 MW MCS-aligned charging systems for US ports, rail yards, and mines

timing_source_assessment.window_date: commercial deployment 2025-2030 and full cargo-equipment transition goal in 2030
timing_source_assessment.product_job_linkage: The plan requires charging and utility upgrades, but its quantitative design uses 50 kW DC chargers and recommends port ownership.
timing_source_assessment.reason: Real charging demand, wrong power/interface/product boundary and adverse to a merchant 1.5-6 MW MCS cabinet.

timing_source_assessment.independent_event: Port of Long Beach Pier A charging project
timing_source_assessment.window_date: permit posted May 2026; approximately 28 months of construction, reaching 2028
timing_source_assessment.product_job_linkage: Exact port charging infrastructure, but 166 Level-2/Level-3 chargers and dedicated substations rather than MCS or a 1.5-6 MW rugged dispenser.
timing_source_assessment.reason: The project is in-window and named but purchases a materially different distributed charging architecture.

records.g7_rationale: Fresh official records prove port electrification through 2030 but also disprove the preserved product mapping: the named ports plan dozens to hundreds of 50 kW/Level-2/Level-3 chargers with port-owned substations, not a merchant 1.5-6 MW MCS system. Counting these sources would silently replace the product. No named post-launch US rail or mine MCS procurement was found.
records.window_risk: Port grants deploy before launch; ABB, Siemens, Kempower, Wabtec, Caterpillar, utilities, EPCs, and vehicle OEMs can bundle the charging stack, interconnection, warranty, and service.

G1.rationale: Current EPA Clean Ports awards and Union Pacific orders prove real charging/equipment demand, though they do not prove this exact merchant product.

G4.rationale: ABB, Siemens, Kempower, Wabtec, Caterpillar, utilities, EPCs, and in-house builds are named; rugged fleet integration is non-cosmetic but weakly defensible.

G6.rationale: US industrial base case with NEC/UL/NFPA, interconnection, cable thermal, and IEC TS 63379 work; no export route is required.

records.market_route: Paid FEED through a port, railroad, or mine with an explicit merchant-prime boundary; do not count generic port electrification or OEM-owned systems as a product route.

decisive_experiment.title: Paid multi-segment FEED and merchant-channel gate
decisive_experiment.dependency: No assumed partner access; counterparty data and payment are outcomes.
decisive_experiment.pass_bar: Two counterparties each pay at least $20,000 or sign funded pilots; one pilot begins by 2029; service-adjusted gross margin exceeds 25 percent; vehicle OEM accepts merchant-prime boundary.
decisive_experiment.kill_bar: No payer, every prospect requires OEM prime, margin below 25 percent, or no prelaunch pilot.

proposed_score_change.reason: The new sources reinforce current infrastructure demand but worsen exact-product and merchant-channel confidence; no additional numeric deduction is needed beyond the literal P5 score.
